app_summary.text: Music library, player and LAN sync
app_summary.note: The app's one-line description: in the About box, and on Linux in the applications menu and software centres.

shared.name: Name

unknown_value.note: Stands in for a missing artist, album or title.

title.note: A track's title, as a field or column name.

tracks_title.note: Heading of a list of tracks.

track_byline.note: Two names joined by a dash: under a track's title, its artist and album; in the window title, the track and its artist.

separator_dot.note: Between the parts of a summary, e.g. "1997 · 12 tracks · 47 min".

import_list_separator.note: Between the items of a list, e.g. "12 imported, 3 skipped".

duration_minutes.note: A total playing time under an hour.

duration_hours_minutes.note: A total playing time of an hour or more.

section_singles.note: Heading of an artist's singles on their page: their tracks that are the only track of their album in the library, or on no album.

section_recents.note: Heading of the albums, playlists and artists last played, on any device: in the sidebar, or on the phone's main screen.

recent_remove_menu.note: On a recent's menu (right-click in the sidebar, long press on the phone): takes it out of Recents, on every device, until it's next played.

recents_clear_menu.note: On a recent's menu: empties Recents, on every device.

section_home.note: The sidebar's first page, above Search; not available yet, so it's greyed out.

search_placeholder.text: Search albums, artists, tracks and playlists
search_placeholder.note: Placeholder of the Search page's search box.

shuffle.note: Button above a list of tracks that plays them in a random order; also the shuffle toggle's name for accessibility.

shuffle_albums.note: Button on an album group: plays its albums in a random order, each album's tracks in order.

shuffle_tracks.note: Button on an album group: plays all its albums' tracks in a random order.

shuffle_on.note: Tooltip of the shuffle toggle in the now-playing bar while it's on.

shuffle_off.note: Tooltip of the shuffle toggle in the now-playing bar while it's off.

seek.note: The seek bar's name for accessibility.

now_playing_artist.note: After the track's title in the now-playing bar, dimmed: its artist.

volume_level.note: Shown for a moment in place of the track in the now-playing bar after the volume changes from the keyboard; on Windows also the volume slider's name for accessibility. {0} is 0 to 100.

volume_muted.note: Shown for a moment in place of the track in the now-playing bar after the sound is muted from the keyboard.

volume.note: The speaker button at the right of the header bar, which opens the volume slider: its tooltip and name for accessibility; also the slider's name for accessibility.

mute.note: Tooltip and accessibility name of the speaker button beside the volume slider, while the sound is on.

unmute.note: Tooltip and accessibility name of the speaker button beside the volume slider, while the sound is muted.

tooltip_shortcut.note: A button's tooltip with its keyboard shortcut, e.g. "Next track (Ctrl+Right)". {0} is the button's name, {1} the shortcut.

about_title.note: Title of the About box (F1); on Linux also its entry in the keyboard shortcuts list. {0} is the app's name.

no_playlists_text.text: Right-click a track and choose Add to playlist to start one, or make an empty one with New playlist.
no_playlists_text.note: The Playlists page while there are none. Add to playlist is the track menu's item; New playlist is the page's + button.

no_playable_playlists_title.note: The Playlists page when the library has playlists but none has a track on this device (the others are hidden).

shared.no_playable_playlists_text: This library contains playlists, but none of them have tracks on this device.

pair_with_device_menu.note: Button on the empty Albums page of a computer that isn't paired yet: lists the devices nearby to pair with.

add_device_by_address_menu.note: Last item of the Pair with a device… menu; opens the Add device dialog.

shared.library_location_text: Opening another library switches to the library in that folder, or starts an empty one there; music you've already imported stays where it is. Moving the library takes its music and database to a new, empty folder.

library_move_choose.text: Choose an empty folder to move the library to
library_move_choose.note: Title of the folder picker that Move library… opens.

library_move_cant_title.note: Heading of the message saying why the chosen folder won't do; the user then picks another.

shared.library_move_same_folder: The library is already in that folder.

library_move_inside.text: That folder is inside the library. Choose one outside it.
library_move_inside.note: The chosen folder is one of the library's own folders.

library_move_contains.text: That folder holds the library. Choose an empty folder somewhere else.
library_move_contains.note: The library's folder is inside the chosen folder.

library_move_not_empty.text: {0} isn't empty. Choose an empty folder, or make a new one.

library_move_not_writable.text: Can't write to {0}. Choose another folder.

library_move_no_space.text: There isn't enough room there: the library needs {0} and the drive has {1} free.

library_move_title.note: Title of the window that shows the move's progress.

library_move_wait.text: Please wait. The library opens again in its new folder when the move is done.
library_move_wait.note: Under the progress bar while the library moves; the window can't be closed.

library_move_progress.note: {0} and {1} count the files moved so far and in all; {2} and {3} are sizes, e.g. "12.5 MB of 3.2 GB".

library_move_checking.note: The files are copied; the database is being opened in its new place.

library_move_removing.note: The library has moved; its files are being removed from the old folder.

library_move_undoing.text: Couldn't finish the move. Putting things back…
library_move_undoing.note: The partial copy is being removed; the library stays where it was.

library_move_failed.text: Couldn't move the library ({0}). It's still in {1}.
library_move_failed.note: {0} is the reason, {1} the old folder.

library_move_failed_file.text: Couldn't move the library: {0} couldn't be copied ({1}). It's still in {2}.
library_move_failed_file.note: {0} is a file, {1} the reason, {2} the old folder.

library_move_left_behind.one: The library has moved, but {0:d} file couldn't be removed from {1}. You can delete it yourself.
library_move_left_behind.other: The library has moved, but {0:d} files couldn't be removed from {1}. You can delete them yourself.

shared.settings_save_failed: Couldn't save the setting; the old folder will be used next time.

new_playlist_track_away.text: This track isn't on this computer, so the playlist won't show on the Playlists page here until one of its tracks is.
new_playlist_track_away.note: Under the name box when making a playlist for a track (Add to playlist) that has no file on this computer: a playlist whose tracks have no file here is hidden from the Playlists page.

playlist_menu.note: The menu button on a playlist's track list: its tooltip, and its name for accessibility.

playlist_delete_title.note: {0} is the name of what's deleted: a playlist, album group, album or track.

shared.playlist_delete_text: Its tracks stay in the library.
shared.playlist_add_failed: Couldn't add the track to the playlist

go_to_album.note: On a track's menu: opens the page of the album it's on.

go_to_artist.note: On a track's menu: opens the page of the artist it's credited to.

shared.album_group_delete_text: Its albums stay in the library.
shared.album_group_add_failed: Couldn't add the album to the album group
shared.album_group_remove_failed: Couldn't remove the album from the album group

delete_from_library_menu.note: On an album's or track's menu (not an artist's): deletes it, and its files, from the library on every device, unlike Remove from playlist or Remove from this PC (this computer, this phone).

delete_no_files_text.text: It has no files on this device. It will be removed from the library on all your devices.
delete_no_files_text.note: Under "Delete “{0}”?", for an album or track that's only on other devices.

shared.delete_failed: Couldn't delete it from the library

delete_restored.note: Shown for a moment once deleted tracks' files are back from the Recycle Bin or Trash, and the tracks are back in the library.

remove_here_files.one: Its file is removed here. It stays in the library and on your other devices.
remove_here_files.other: Its {0:d} files are removed here. It stays in the library and on your other devices.
remove_here_files.note: Under "Remove “{0}” from this PC?" (this computer, this phone): an album's or artist's files on this device.

remove_here_no_files.text: It has no files here, and won't be synced here. It stays in the library and on your other devices.
remove_here_no_files.note: Under "Remove “{0}” from this PC?" (this computer, this phone), for an album or artist with no files on this device.

remove_here_kept.one: {0:d} file imported here stays until an archive holds a copy.
remove_here_kept.other: {0:d} files imported here stay until an archive holds a copy.
remove_here_kept.note: After remove_here_files: originals imported on this device are kept until an archive device (one that keeps the whole library) has verified copies.

remove_here_in_use.one: {0:d} file couldn't be removed here. Is it open in another app? Sync removes it later.
remove_here_in_use.other: {0:d} files couldn't be removed here. Are they open in another app? Sync removes them later.

shared.remove_here_failed: Couldn't remove it from this device
shared.sync_here_failed: Couldn't sync it to this device again

no_album_groups_text.text: Right-click an album and choose Add to album group to start one, or make an empty one with New album group.
no_album_groups_text.note: The Album groups page while there are none. Add to album group is the album menu's item; New album group is the page's + button.

album_group_empty_title.note: An album group's page when the group has no albums on it.

album_group_empty_text.text: Right-click an album and choose Add to album group, then this group, to add it here.
album_group_empty_text.note: An empty album group's page. Add to album group is the album menu's item.

album_group_menu.note: The menu button on an album group's page: its tooltip, and its name for accessibility.

not_on_device.note: A track with no file on this device: its tooltip, or its status for accessibility.

smart_playlist.note: A playlist whose tracks are chosen by a rule, e.g. "the 100 most played"; under its name, and in search results and recents.

smart_album_group.note: An album group whose albums are chosen by a rule, e.g. "albums added recently".

reshuffle.note: Button on a smart playlist or smart album group that's in a random order: picks a new random order.

smart_list_empty_title.note: A smart playlist's or smart album group's page when its rule picks nothing.

shared.smart_list_empty_text: Nothing in your library matches this list's rule

smart_field_title.note: A smart list rule's field, in the rule editor's field picker; the smart_field_* strings are labels, capitalised on their own.

smart_field_track_count.note: An album's number of tracks, as a smart album group rule's field.

smart_field_plays.note: How many times something was played, as a smart list rule's field.

smart_field_singles.note: A smart list rule's field: whether a track is a single (the only track of its album in the library, or on no album), or an album is one (it has one track).

smart_field_on_device.note: A smart list rule's field: whether a track or album has a file on this device.

smart_field_format.note: A file format such as FLAC, as a smart list rule's field.

smart_field_random.note: In a smart list's sort order picker: a random order.

smart_field_title_in_text.note: A smart list rule's field inside a sentence describing the rule, e.g. "title contains “love”"; the smart_field_*_in_text strings are {0} of the smart_cond_* strings.

smart_field_plays_in_text.note: Inside a sentence describing a smart list's rule, e.g. "play count is less than 3".

smart_field_last_played_in_text.note: Inside a sentence describing a smart list's rule, e.g. "last played is in the last 30 days".

smart_op_is.note: A smart list rule's operator, in the rule editor's picker after a field, e.g. Genre [is] Jazz. The smart_op_* strings are all pickers' entries.

smart_op_between.note: Followed by two values, e.g. Year [is between] 1990 and 1999.

smart_op_within.note: Followed by a number of days, e.g. Last played [is in the last] 30 days.

smart_value_yes.note: A smart list rule's value for a yes-or-no field, e.g. On this device [Yes].

smart_tracks_where.note: A smart playlist's rule as a sentence. {0} is its conditions, e.g. "genre contains “jazz”, and play count is less than 3".

smart_albums_where.note: A smart album group's rule as a sentence; {0} is its conditions.

smart_all_tracks.note: A smart playlist's rule that picks every track.

smart_all_albums.note: A smart album group's rule that picks every album.

smart_no_albums.note: A smart album group's rule that can't pick any album.

smart_quoted.note: A text value in a smart list's rule, e.g. genre contains “jazz”.

smart_and_two.note: Two of a smart list rule's conditions that must all be true.

smart_and_more.note: Joins all but the last of three or more conditions that must all be true: {0} is the first ones.

smart_and_last.note: Joins the last of three or more conditions that must all be true: {0} is the others.

smart_or_two.note: Two of a smart list rule's conditions, either of which will do.

smart_or_more.note: Joins all but the last of three or more conditions, any of which will do.

smart_or_last.note: Joins the last of three or more conditions, any of which will do.

smart_parens.note: A group of conditions inside a smart list's rule.

smart_none_of.note: In a smart list's rule: none of these conditions is true. {0} is the conditions joined with "or".

smart_not_all_of.note: In a smart list's rule: at least one of these conditions is false. {0} is the conditions joined with "and".

smart_always.note: An empty group of conditions that's always true, inside a smart list's rule.

smart_never.note: An empty group of conditions that's never true, inside a smart list's rule.

smart_cond_is.note: A smart list rule's condition. In smart_cond_*, {0} is a field (smart_field_*_in_text) and {1} a value, e.g. “jazz” or 1969.

smart_cond_between.note: {1} and {2} are the lowest and highest values, which are included.

smart_cond_within.note: {1} is a length of time (smart_days or smart_weeks), e.g. "last played is in the last 30 days".

smart_cond_never_played.note: A smart list rule's condition: Last played is empty.

smart_cond_played.note: A smart list rule's condition: Last played isn't empty.

smart_cond_on_device.note: A smart list rule's condition: a track or album has a file on this device.

smart_cond_single.note: A smart playlist rule's condition: a track is the only track of its album in the library, or has no album.

smart_cond_singles_album.note: A smart album group rule's condition: an album has only one track in the library.

smart_cond_format.note: A smart list rule's condition. {0} is a file format, e.g. FLAC.

smart_cond_in_playlist.note: A smart playlist rule's condition. {0} is the playlist's name in quotes (smart_quoted).

smart_cond_in_deleted_playlist.note: A smart playlist rule's condition naming a playlist that's since been deleted, so nothing matches it.

shared.smart_cond_not_in_deleted_playlist: it isn't in a deleted playlist

smart_cond_in_group.note: A smart list rule's condition: the album is, or a track's album is, in this album group. {0} is the group's name in quotes (smart_quoted).

shared.smart_cond_not_in_group: it isn't in the album group {0}

smart_cond_in_deleted_group.text: it's in a deleted album group
smart_cond_in_deleted_group.note: A smart list rule's condition naming an album group that's since been deleted, so nothing matches it.

shared.smart_cond_not_in_deleted_group: it isn't in a deleted album group

smart_days.note: A length of time in a smart list's rule, e.g. "in the last 30 days".

smart_weeks.note: A length of time in a smart list's rule, e.g. "in the last 2 weeks".

smart_date.note: A date in a smart list's rule: {0} is the day of the month, {1} the month's name (smart_month_*), {2} the year, e.g. "March 12, 2025".

smart_order_then.note: A smart list's sort order, sorting by {0} and then, where that's the same, by {1}.

smart_order_random.note: A smart list in a random order, after the rule's conditions, e.g. "All tracks · shuffled".

smart_order_title_asc.note: A smart list's sort order. The smart_order_* strings go after the rule's conditions, e.g. "All tracks · title A to Z · 10 tracks", and in the editor's sort picker.

shared.add_device_text: Enter the address of a device on your network. It will show a code to enter next.
shared.import_running_text: Wait for the current import to finish first.
shared.import_no_library_text: The library could not be opened, so nothing can be imported.

import_start_failed.note: {0} is the reason, e.g. "out of memory".

shared.import_stop_text: Anything already imported stays in your library.

import_status_review.text: {0}. {1}: click one to choose a match.
import_status_review.note: {0} is how many were imported, e.g. "12 imported"; {1} how many need a decision, e.g. "3 need a decision".

import_status_finished.note: How many were imported, skipped and failed, e.g. "12 imported", "1 skipped", "0 failed".

import_needs_decision.note: An import item's state, and the heading of the items in that state.

import_state_replaced.note: An import item whose files replaced the library's lower-quality copies of the same release.

import_state_duplicate.note: An import item that was skipped because the library already has it in equal or better quality.

import_state_added_missing.note: An import item of a release the library already had: only the tracks the library lacked were added.

import_group_active.note: Heading of the import items still being matched or written.

import_single.note: An import item that is one track rather than an album.

import_existing_tags.note: An item imported with the tags its files already had.

import_match_year.note: A MusicBrainz match: artist, album or title, and year.

import_match_into.note: A single's match: the release it comes from, then the track.

shared.import_item_busy: This item is busy. Try again in a moment.

import_review_album.note: {0} is the artist, {1} the album, {2} how many files it has.

import_search_wider.note: Button in the review of an imported album or track: searches MusicBrainz (the online music database) again using other clues from the files and the folder name, such as catalogue numbers, the tracks' artists and the record label.

import_track_missing.note: A track of the chosen match that no file was matched to.

import_not_matched.note: A file that no track of the chosen match fits.

import_other_item_file.note: In an import's track list, a file from the same folder that was grouped as an item of its own (and maybe already imported as that). {0} is that item's album, or the track's title.

import_use_as_track.note: Menu item for a missing track and a file selected together in an import's track list: the file becomes that track, and is tagged and filed as it. On Linux also the heading of a missing track's menu of files. {0} is the track's number, e.g. "3", or "2-3" for disc 2, track 3.

import_use_as_track_hint.text: To fix a missing track, click it and choose its file.
import_use_as_track_hint.note: Under an import's track list when some tracks are missing and some files weren't matched. Clicking a missing track (or pressing Enter on it) lists the files it can take.

import_choose_file.note: Button on a missing track in an import's track list (Linux), and the hint in its File column (Windows, followed by a dropdown arrow): opens a menu of the files that could be that track.

col_confidence.note: How sure an import match is, as a percentage: a column heading, and the tooltip of the percentage.

import_state_moved.note: An import item whose files were all made tracks of another album with "Use as track", or that was one disc of an album and was joined to its other discs.

import_joined_discs.one: Joined {0:d} disc into one album: check that it belongs.
import_joined_discs.other: Joined {0:d} discs into one album: check that they belong together.
import_joined_discs.note: Why an import item waits for the user: items that looked like the discs of one album ("Title Disc1", "Title Disc2") were made one album, matched to a release on MusicBrainz with that many discs. {0} is the number of discs; always 2 or more.

import_offline.text: You're offline, so music can't be tagged from MusicBrainz until you're back online.
import_offline.note: Banner on the Import page when the internet (MusicBrainz, the online music database used to tag files) can't be reached.

import_skip_tagging.note: Button on the offline banner: imports the remaining items with the tags their files already have, without looking them up on MusicBrainz.

shared.import_error_write_tags: Couldn't write tags to a file (is it read-only or open elsewhere?)
shared.import_error_mkdir: Couldn't create a folder in the library
shared.import_error_rename: Couldn't rename a file in the library
shared.import_error_copy: Couldn't copy a file into the library
shared.import_error_copy_full: Couldn't copy a file into the library (is the disk full?)
shared.import_error_no_name: Couldn't find a free file name in the library
shared.import_error_move: Couldn't move a file within the library

import_error_zip_bad.text: Couldn't open the zip (is it damaged or password-protected?)
import_error_zip_bad.note: An import item for a .zip file that couldn't be extracted.

import_error_zip_too_big.text: The zip is too big to import (over {0:d} GB unzipped)
import_error_zip_too_big.note: An import item for a .zip file; {0} is the limit in gigabytes.

import_error_zip_session_too_big.text: Too much to unzip in one import (over {0:d} GB of zips in all): import this zip on its own
import_error_zip_session_too_big.note: An import item for a .zip file left out because the zips imported together with it already hold the limit; {0} is the limit in gigabytes.

import_error_zip_space.text: Not enough free space to unzip it
import_error_zip_space.note: An import item for a .zip file that wouldn't fit on the disk once extracted.

import_error_zip_write.text: Couldn't unzip it (is the disk full?)
import_error_zip_write.note: An import item for a .zip file whose files couldn't be written out.

import_error_long_path.text: Couldn't read this file (its path is 260 characters or longer)
import_error_long_path.note: An import item for one audio file that couldn't be read, whose full path (folders and file name) is longer than Windows allows by default.

status_ok.note: Status reasons appear inside other messages, e.g. "Couldn't start the import (out of memory).", so they start in lower case.

status_auth.note: The scrobbling service (e.g. Last.fm) refused the sign-in, the session or the app's API key.

pair.note: A button or screen title for pairing with another device.

sync.note: Pairing and syncing between devices: a menu item, screen title or notification channel name.

pair_wrong_code.note: While pairing, on both devices: the code was typed wrong on the device asking to pair. {0} is tries_left.

shared.pair_show_code: To pair, enter this code on {0}.

paired_peer_text.text: {0} is paired, but no music syncs to it yet. Choose what {0} holds, then press Sync now.
paired_peer_text.note: After pairing, on the device that was already set up. {0} is the device that just joined, which copies no files until its sync settings are chosen and Sync now is pressed.

choose_what_to_sync.note: Opens a device's sync settings: the albums, artists, playlists and album groups it holds. On the phone, in its sync settings; on a computer, the button under "none of them have tracks on this device" (this computer's page), and after pairing (the page of the device that just joined).

archive_explainer.text: {0} is the **archive** device. It holds the original copies of all of your music. This can only be changed if another device chooses to be an archive and has a full sync of this library.
archive_explainer.note: Shown once, after this device joined a sync group. {0} is the archive's name. Keep the ** around the word for archive: it's shown in bold where possible, and the ** themselves never show.

archive_explainer_several.one: {0} and {1:d} other device are **archive** devices. They hold the original copies of all of your music. This can only be changed if another device chooses to be an archive and has a full sync of this library.
archive_explainer_several.other: {0} and {1:d} other devices are **archive** devices. They hold the original copies of all of your music. This can only be changed if another device chooses to be an archive and has a full sync of this library.
archive_explainer_several.note: As archive_explainer, when the group has several archives. {0} is the first one's name, {1} how many others there are. Keep the ** around the word for archive.

pair_create_library.note: Button after pairing failed because both devices have music: picks a folder for a new, empty library on this device.

pair_new_library_hint.text: To pair anyway, create a new, empty library here. Your music stays where it is, and Open another library in Settings switches back to it.
pair_new_library_hint.note: Follows the library mismatch message, above the Create a new library button.

library_folder_new.text: Choose an empty folder for the new library
library_folder_new.note: Title of the folder picker opened by Create a new library.

library_not_empty.text: That folder isn't empty. Choose an empty folder for the new library.
library_not_empty.note: After Create a new library, when the folder picked has files in it.

pair_again_text.text: The new, empty library is open. Pair with {0} again?
pair_again_text.note: After Create a new library switched to it. {0} is the device the pairing failed with.

pair_again.note: Button: asks the same device to pair again.

shared.pair_wrong_code_too_often: The code was wrong too many times.
shared.pair_busy: {0} is pairing with another device. Try again in a moment.
shared.pair_unreachable: Couldn't reach {0}. Check that Kithsong is open on it and that both are on the same network.

pair_merge_title.note: Title while pairing two devices that both have music, on the device whose library is merged into the other's. It confirms with Merge, or cancels.

pair_merge_text.text: Both devices have music. {0} has the larger library ({1}; this device has {2}), so it's kept, and the music here is merged into it.
pair_merge_text.note: On the device whose library is merged. {0} is the other device; {1} and {2} are track counts (the tracks string), there and here.

pair_merge_backup.text: Your library here is saved as a backup file in its folder first, then replaced by the merged one. Its edit history isn't carried over.

pair_merge_scrobble.text: Last.fm user {0} will be signed out here; {1}'s account is used instead.
pair_merge_scrobble.note: After pair_merge_text, when both devices are signed in to Last.fm. {0} is this device's Last.fm user name, {1} the other device.

pair_merge_forget.one: {1}, paired with this device, will be forgotten and has to pair again to sync with it.
pair_merge_forget.other: {0:d} devices paired with this one will be forgotten and have to pair again to sync with it: {1}.
pair_merge_forget.note: After pair_merge_text, when the device whose library is merged is in a sync group of its own. {1} lists the devices' names.

pair_merge_button.note: Button: agrees to merge this device's library into the other device's, and goes on pairing.

pair_merge_kept_text.text: Both devices have music. The library here is the larger one ({1}; {0} has {2}), so it's kept, and {0}'s music is merged into it once {0} agrees.
pair_merge_kept_text.note: While pairing, on the device whose library is kept. {0} is the other device; {1} and {2} are track counts (the tracks string), here and there.

pair_merge_confirmed.text: The libraries will be merged once the devices are paired.

firewall_rule_description.text: Lets Kithsong on your other devices find this PC and sync with it on the local network.
firewall_rule_description.note: Description of the rule shown in Windows Firewall's settings.

smart_new_playlist_menu.note: Menu item on the Playlists page and the sidebar's Playlists: opens the smart playlist editor.

smart_new_group_menu.note: Menu item on the Album Groups page and the sidebar's Album Groups.

smart_edit_menu.note: Menu item on a smart playlist or smart album group: opens its rule in the editor.

smart_playlist_menu.note: The menu button on a smart playlist's track list: its tooltip, and its name for accessibility.

smart_group_menu.note: The menu button on a smart album group's page: its tooltip, and its name for accessibility.

windows.smart_save_failed: Couldn't save the smart list's rule

smart_preset_heading.note: Above the choice of ready-made rules a new smart playlist or smart album group can start from.

smart_preset_recent.note: A ready-made smart playlist rule, and the new list's name: tracks added in the last 30 days, newest first.

smart_preset_least_played.note: A ready-made smart playlist rule: the 100 least played tracks on this device.

smart_preset_not_played.note: A ready-made smart playlist rule: tracks not played in the last 180 days.

smart_preset_flac.note: A ready-made smart playlist rule: tracks with a FLAC file on this device.

windows.smart_preset_not_played_albums: Albums not played in a while

smart_preset_blank.note: Starting a smart list with no conditions of its own.

next.note: Button: goes on to the next step, e.g. from the ready-made rules to the editor.

smart_tracks_matching.note: In the smart playlist editor, before a choice of all, any or none, then smart_of_these: "Tracks matching [all] of these:".

smart_albums_matching.note: As smart_tracks_matching, for a smart album group.

smart_group_matching.note: At the start of a group of conditions inside a smart list's rule: "Matching [any] of these:".

smart_match_all.note: Picker entry: every condition must be true.

smart_match_any.note: Picker entry: one condition is enough.

smart_match_none.note: Picker entry: no condition may be true.

smart_of_these.note: After the all/any/none picker, e.g. "Tracks matching [all] of these:".

smart_add_condition.note: Button in the smart list editor: adds a condition.

smart_add_group.note: Button in the smart list editor: adds a group of conditions, matching any of them, say.

smart_add_sort.note: Button in the smart list editor: adds another sort order, for ties in the ones before.

smart_sort_by.note: Before the first sort order picker in the smart list editor.

smart_sort_then.note: Before each further sort order picker, e.g. "Sort by [least played first], then [newest added first]".

smart_sorted.note: Smart list editor: the list keeps the sort order above (radio button).

smart_shuffled.note: Smart list editor: the list is in a random order, after any sort order above (radio button).

smart_limit.note: Checkbox in the smart list editor, followed by a number and smart_limit_tracks: "Only the first [10] tracks".

smart_limit_tracks.note: After the number in "Only the first [10] tracks".

smart_limit_albums.note: After the number in "Only the first [10] albums".

smart_unit_days.note: Picker after a number in a condition, e.g. Last played [isn't in the last] [180] [days].

smart_between_and.note: Between two numbers, e.g. Year [is between] [1990] and [1999].

smart_duration_cue.note: Grey hint in an empty box for a length of time, minutes and seconds.

smart_deleted_member.note: In a condition's picker of playlists or album groups: one the rule names that's since been deleted.

smart_hint_device.note: Under a smart list condition on files (On this device, Format): other devices may pick different tracks.

smart_hint_missing_tracks.note: Tooltip on a negative condition such as Genre [isn't] Rock. {0} is the field inside a sentence (smart_field_*_in_text), e.g. genre.

smart_needs_value.note: Under a smart list condition whose value is missing or can't be read, e.g. a number box left empty.

smart_prefix_count.note: Beside each top-level condition: how many match it and every condition above it. {0} is a number.

smart_in_list.note: After smart_tracks_match when the list keeps only the first few, e.g. "142 tracks match · 10 in the list".

smart_counting.note: While the smart list editor works out how many tracks match.

smart_preview.note: Heading of the list of what a smart list's rule picks now, in its editor.

smart_read_only.text: This rule can't be edited here: it was made by a newer version of Kithsong, or it uses conditions this editor can't show. It stays as it is.
smart_read_only.note: In the smart list editor, above the rule as a sentence.

smart_field_name.note: Name for accessibility of a smart list condition's first picker, e.g. Genre.

smart_op_name.note: Name for accessibility of a smart list condition's second picker, e.g. contains.

smart_value_name.note: Name for accessibility of a smart list condition's value, e.g. jazz.

smart_value_high_name.note: Name for accessibility of the second number in "is between 1990 and 1999".

smart_unit_name.note: Name for accessibility of the days/weeks/months picker.

smart_group_mode_name.note: Name for accessibility of a group's all/any/none picker.

smart_match_name.note: Name for accessibility of the rule's all/any/none picker.

smart_sort_name.note: Name for accessibility of a sort order picker in the smart list editor.

smart_limit_count_name.note: Name for accessibility of the number in "Only the first [10] tracks".

scrobble_sign_in_short.note: Button beside the Last.fm account in Settings; opens Last.fm in the browser.

jump_to_named_section.note: An accessibility action on the main screen's section headings. {0} is a section, such as Albums.

album_byline_year.note: Track list screen: an album's artist and year.

album_menu.note: The menu button on an album's page; for accessibility.

track_menu.note: The menu button on the player, for the track playing; for accessibility.

seek_state.note: The seekbar's state for accessibility: elapsed time of total time.

edit_playlist.note: Button on a playlist's or album group's page that shows the controls to reorder and remove its tracks or albums.

add_to_album_group_menu.note: On an album's menu: opens the list of album groups to add it to.

playlist_reorder.note: A playlist track's or album group album's drag handle, for accessibility.

delete_permanently_text.one: {0:d} file will be deleted for good and removed from the library on all your devices. This phone has no trash to restore it from.
delete_permanently_text.other: {0:d} files will be deleted for good and removed from the library on all your devices. This phone has no trash to restore them from.
delete_permanently_text.note: Under "Delete “{0}”?"; the files are an album's or track's, and its cover.

delete_kept.one: {0:d} track couldn't be deleted, so it's still in the library.
delete_kept.other: {0:d} tracks couldn't be deleted, so they're still in the library.

remove_from_this_phone.note: On an album's or artist's menu: removes its files from this phone only; it stays in the library and on the other devices.

sync_to_this_phone.note: On the menu of an album or artist removed from this phone: syncs it here again.

android.remove_from_this_phone_back: To get it back, choose Sync to this phone from its menu.
android.empty_text_import: Import music from this phone, or pair it with Kithsong on a computer, under Sync, to bring your music here.

empty_text_choose.text: This phone is paired, but none of your music is on it yet. Choose what to sync to it, or import music from this phone.
empty_text_choose.note: The empty main screen while this phone is in a sync group (its sync settings hold nothing, or nothing has arrived yet). Above the Import and Choose what to sync buttons.

import_folder.note: Import menu item: opens the system's folder picker.

import_files.note: Import menu item: opens the system's file picker, for audio files and .zip files such as Bandcamp downloads.

import_files_folder.note: Folder name given to audio files picked or shared one by one, while they're imported; it can show in an import item's name.

import_added.one: {0:d} shared file added to the import
import_added.other: {0:d} shared files added to the import
import_added.note: Toast when files are shared with the app while an import runs: they're imported after what it's already doing.

import_copying_files.note: Files copied so far of those picked. The plural follows {1}.

import_batch.note: Which of the picked album folders or zips is being imported; they're imported one at a time.

import_no_match.text: {0}. No sure match for the rest
import_no_match.note: After how many were imported, e.g. "12 imported".

import_no_match_reason.text: {0}. No sure match for the rest ({1})
import_no_match_reason.note: After how many were imported, e.g. "12 imported"; then why, e.g. "Couldn't reach MusicBrainz".

import_problem.note: An album that failed to import, in the list after an import: its name, then why, e.g. "Couldn't reach MusicBrainz".

import_not_music.note: A picked or shared file that was left out of the import. {0} is its name.

import_copy_failed.note: A picked file that couldn't be copied for the import. {0} is its name.

android.import_read_failed: Couldn't read everything that was picked

import_no_space.text: {0}: not enough free space ({1} needed twice over)
import_no_space.note: A picked folder or zip that was left out. {0} is its name, {1} its size, e.g. "1.2 GB": it's copied in, then into the library.

import_review_open.note: Button on the import card: opens the list of items waiting for a decision.

import_tags_all.note: Imports every item waiting for a decision with the tags its files already have.

android.import_review_empty: Nothing is waiting for a decision.

import_match_details.note: How well a MusicBrainz release matches the files, e.g. "85% match".

import_search_title.text: Album, or track for a single
import_search_title.note: Field of the import's search: what to search MusicBrainz for.

android.settings_sync_text: The devices this phone syncs with, and pairing new ones
android.permission_notifications_denied: Not allowed. Playback controls still show, sync progress doesn't
android.storage_art_cache_size: {0} of covers sized for the screen

licenses.note: Settings entry, and the title of its screen: the third-party libraries in the app and their licences.

android.licenses_text: The libraries Kithsong is built with

licenses_native.note: Heading on the licences screen: the C libraries the native core is built from.

licenses_overview.note: Licences screen: the list of every third-party library, its version and licence (LICENSES.md).

licenses_android.note: Heading on the licences screen: the Android/Kotlin libraries.

android.this_phone_in_group: It syncs with the other devices in its group whenever both are on the same network.
android.this_phone_alone: Not paired yet. Pair it with Kithsong on a computer to sync your library.
android.sync_now_text: With every device in the group on this network

device_files_checked.note: When a device last verified its music files.

device_last_session.note: How the last sync with a device went.

session_files.note: Music files in a sync session. The plural follows {0}.

progress_bytes.note: Sizes, e.g. "12 MB received, 0 B sent".

android.profile_no_group: Once this phone is in a group, choose here what it holds.
android.profile_archive_locked: This phone can stop being an archive once another archive has checked that it holds the whole library.

estimate_tracks.note: What a device would hold: how many tracks, and their size, e.g. "1,200 tracks, 8 GB".

estimate_over_budget.text: Doesn't fit even as Opus 64 kbps: {0} too big. Nothing syncs until it fits.

estimate_limit.note: What a device's music must fit in: its storage limit or free space. {0} is a size.

estimate_free.note: A device's free space. {0} is a size.

android.device_in_other_group: Syncs with other devices. Remove it from them to pair it here
android.devices_looking: Looking for devices on this network
android.devices_looking_text: Open Kithsong on your computer. If it doesn't show up, add it by its address
android.add_device_by_address_text: For networks where devices can't find each other
android.leave_group_text: Stop syncing with these devices. The music on this phone stays
android.leave_group_confirm: This phone stops syncing with {0}. To sync again, pair it again.

pair_code_description.note: The pairing code read out digit by digit, e.g. "Code 1 2 3 4 5 6".

android.self_in_group: This phone. It syncs with the devices below whenever both are on the same network.
android.self_alone: This phone. Pair it with Kithsong on a computer to sync your library.
android.sync_not_on_wifi: Not on Wi-Fi. Sync reaches devices on the same local network.
android.sync_other_library: The library on this phone isn't the one this group syncs, so only the list of devices syncs.

paired_text.text: This phone is paired with {0}, but no music syncs to it yet. Choose what this phone holds, then press Sync now.
paired_text.note: After pairing, on the phone that just joined. {0} is the other device.

android.pair_in_group: {0} already syncs with other devices. Remove it from them, or this phone from its group, first.
android.pair_library_mismatch: This phone and {0} each have music of their own. A device can only join with an empty library.
android.pair_library_mismatch_incoming: {0} asked to pair, but it and this phone each have music of their own. A device can only join with an empty library.
android.sync_notification_see_code: Open Kithsong to see the code

sync_notification_files.note: Audio files received so far of those to fetch, under "Syncing with …". The plural follows {1}.

sync_notification_files_sent.note: Audio files sent so far of those the other device is fetching from this phone, under "Syncing with …". The plural follows {1}.

android.sync_error_open: Couldn't open this phone's sync data

merge_tracks_deleted.note: Tracks the library had in the same or better quality: this phone's copy was deleted (Android has no trash). One item of merge_tracks' list.

wear.watch_empty_text: No music on this watch yet. Pair it under Sync to add some.

watch_pair_refused.note: Title of the watch's screen when it turned down a pairing request.

watch_pair_waiting.text: Add {0} under Devices on your computer, or under Sync on your phone.

watch_enter_code.note: {0} is the name of the device asking to pair.

watch_syncing.note: The plural follows {1}, the number of tracks to sync.

watch_paired_text.text: Paired with {0}. Choose what this watch holds on one of them.
watch_paired_text.note: {0} is the list of paired devices' names.

wear.watch_refused_in_group: This watch is already paired with other devices. Remove it there first.

watch_refused_library_mismatch.text: This watch holds music from a different library than {0}.
watch_refused_library_mismatch.note: {0} is the name of the device asking to pair.

watch_refused_already_paired.text: This watch is already paired with {0}.
watch_refused_already_paired.note: {0} is the name of the device asking to pair.

watch_licenses.note: The watch's Settings entry, and the title of its screen: the third-party libraries in the watch app and their licences.

watch_licenses_native.note: Heading on the watch's licences screen: the C libraries the native core is built from.

watch_licenses_overview.note: The watch's licences screen: the list of every third-party library, its version and licence (LICENSES.md).

watch_licenses_android.note: Heading on the watch's licences screen: the Android/Kotlin libraries.
